about: Guest memory ordering on arm64 hosts (Mac, Android), applied by regen.sh (tools.recomp --mem-order, toolkit tools/recomp/mem_order.py). Each release store is a lock's flag written back to 0 by a plain mov after the owner's writes: on x86-64 those writes are visible first by the architecture, on arm64 only with a store-release. acquire_spin_exits puts an acquire fence after every busy-wait loop the spin-wait matcher recognises (build/xr/recomp/spin_waits.json lists them: DSOUND voice and APU polls, D3D push-buffer and NV2A polls, XPP), so what the loop guards is read after the flag. Audit 2026-11-03, 1-lifter-atomics F1.

release_stores.note: DirtySock NetCrit release (sub_0021C650): the lock flag at +8 of the lock (global 0x41CE70 or the caller's) written 0 after the owner id and count, before RtlLeaveCriticalSection; taken with xchg at 0x0021C5FC/0x0021C610.
The second DirtySock lock (global 0x41CFA0, taken with xchg at 0x0021C767): flag written 0 on the last release before RtlLeaveCriticalSection 0x41CFA4.
The same lock 0x41CFA0 released on the shutdown path, before the LeaveCriticalSection call through edi.
The same lock 0x41CFA0 cleared where the module is torn down (with 0x41CE78), no critical section after it.
